title: Practice: linear functions
intro: Eight questions on gradients and intercepts. Gradients may be fractions — type them like 3/4.

questions.prompt: Write down the gradient and $y$-intercept of each line.
hints: The number in front of $x$ is $m$. Watch $y = 7 - 2x$ — it is written the other way round.
questions.explanation: $m$ is the coefficient of $x$ and $c$ is the constant. $y = 7 - 2x$ is $y = -2x + 7$.

questions.prompt: Find the gradient of the line joining $(1, 3)$ and $(5, 11)$.
Find the gradient of the line joining $(-1, 6)$ and $(3, -2)$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{-8}{4} = -2$. The line goes down from left to right.

questions.prompt: Set the sliders so the line passes through $(0, 1)$ and $(2, 5)$.

hints: It is on the vertical axis.
questions.explanation: The $y$-intercept is where the line crosses the $y$-axis — the value of $c$ in $y = mx + c$.
a: $-4$. b: $-1$. e: $\frac{-4}{2} = -2$. c and d have positive gradients.

questions.prompt: A line has gradient 3 and passes through $(0, -2)$. Write its equation. (Type $y = \dots$)
Using the points $C(0.5, 2)$ and $D(1.5, 4)$ on the line $y = 2x + 1$ gives a different gradient from using $A(0, 1)$ and $B(2, 5)$.
questions.explanation: False. $\frac{2}{1} = 2$, the same as $\frac{4}{2} = 2$. Any two points on a straight line give the same gradient.
